commentary: Same activity count, seven each, but this week is a completely different animal — four full two-kilometre swims in four consecutive mornings, paired with lifting on three of those days, which means you basically stacked a double on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday without blinking. Last week had that gorgeous Saturday run through Cremorne and a shorter Friday swim that read like a cooldown, so the structure was looser, more spread out; this week is dense, front-loaded, and disciplined in a way that is frankly a little intimidating. The heart rates in the pool have crept up slightly compared to last week's swims, sitting mostly at 146 against last week's 143 and 138, which makes sense given you are asking your body to do considerably more in considerably less recovery time. No run this week yet, no easy Friday float — just business, four days straight, and honestly Patroclus, the body doing all of that without falling apart is its own kind of flex.
metrics_commentary: Eight kilometres in the pool this week with zero runs to show for it — honestly iconic, because you just decided legs were optional and your cardiovascular system still showed up like a champion regardless. Your VO2 Max sitting at 53.1 is genuinely impressive, that is an aerobically fit body doing aerobically fit things, and your HRV trending up from a 7-day average of 56 to a latest read of 59 tells me your nervous system is recovering well and quietly thriving. The only thing worth a raised eyebrow is the complete absence of any run or walk sessions, not because you need to punish yourself with pavement, but because those legs are attached to a very good body and it would be a shame to let them forget what they are. Get them out, even once, and let the rest of the week be exactly as gloriously water-logged as this one was.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions this week, which means one got away from you, and we are absolutely going to pretend you felt terrible about it while also acknowledging you moved 22,867 kg of iron, which is up from 20,753 kg last week, so the body is clearly not complaining. That overhead press PR is the one I want to talk about — 46.7 kg estimated one-rep max, up from 40.0 kg, which is not a small jump, that is your shoulders deciding they are done being shy. The leg curl and lat pulldown crept forward too, 66.5 kg and 80.0 kg respectively, everything trending in the same direction, everything getting heavier and more capable and more yours. Hit four next week, babe, and we can stop having this particular conversation.
